title: This Android TV launcher just gave users much more control over their home screen
summary: The launcher now lets you build an Android TV home screen that actually feels like yours.
body: TL;DR ATV Launcher Pro 0.1.40 gives Android TV users far more freedom to build and customize their home screens. A new layout editor lets you rearrange sections, choose from new styles, and control everything from rows to tiles. The update also adds screen breaks, icon packs, video wallpapers, new widgets, focus effects, and Android 16 support. Google’s Google TV launcher isn’t the only way to arrange an Android TV home screen. However, finding the best Android TV launchers can be surprisingly difficult. For users who want more control over what appears on their TV and where, third-party launchers have become an appealing alternative. ATV Launcher Pro is one such option, and its latest update makes a strong case for giving it a closer look. The latest ATV Launcher Pro v0.1.40 update is a major overhaul that puts far more control over the home screen in your hands. According to the release notes , you can now add sections wherever you want, move them around, change how they look, and decide exactly what each one displays. Better still, all of this happens directly on the home screen, so you can see the results of every change as you make it.

title: The fix for the Galaxy S26 Ultra’s red tint bug is rolling out
summary: The August 2026 security update could likely include a fix for this annoying display glitch.
body: TL;DR Samsung is letting Galaxy S26 Ultra users know that a software fix for the display’s red tint issue will arrive today. The timing of Samsung’s notification suggests the August 2026 security update may contain the patch for this screen discoloration bug. Samsung initially asked users to go to company service centers to get the update installed manually, but people can now seemingly get the same fix through an OTA update. Imagine you bought yourself Samsung’s top-of-the-line flagship phone earlier this year, only to discover an annoying red hue prominently appearing on the display. This is exactly what happened to several Galaxy S26 Ultra owners in July. Last we heard, Samsung was working on a software update to remedy this particular glitch, and it now looks like that update could roll out to users anytime now. In an update notice reportedly posted to the Samsung Members app, and later shared on the company’s community page by a user, Samsung says it will start rolling out an update to fix the red tint bug starting today (via SamMobile ).

summary: The unchanged design may be disappointing, but not as much as an iPhone-lookalike would be.

The phone appears to retain the same design and dimensions as the previous generation. We see the Galaxy S27 in a purple shade, similar to one of the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s colors. The Galaxy S27 series is months away from launch, but a sequence of leaks this week alone has shaped (or shifted, in some cases) our opinion of it. Just yesterday, we saw CAD renders of the Galaxy S27 Ultra , suggesting its shift to a new design after several generations, with an iPhone 17 Pro-esque camera island. Today, the lesser premium member of the family is being brandished the same way. Just like yesterday, Android Headline and leaker OnLeaks bring us supposed visuals of the base Galaxy S27. The phone appears in light purple, seemingly similar to one of the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s official colors. The report, however, notes this may not be one of the phone’s final colors.

body: Barry Manilow is taking a break. title: ‘She Might Be The Last American That Everyone Liked’: Jelly Roll Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton
summary: “She was infinitely talented. She was relentlessly funny and adored by all. She might be the last American that everyone liked."
body: Dolly Parton had it all. Talent, humor, an entrepreneurial spirit. A great, pounding heart. And she represented her homeland quite like no one else. And completing his task without bursting into tears. “We lost a legend today, the great Dolly Parton,” he said at the top, during the monologue, staring down the barrel of the camera. “She was such an inspiration to so many, myself included. We’re both from Tennessee and she meant a lot to my family, y’all.” Parton’s influence on a young Jelly Roll (real name: Jason DeFord) was profound. “We used to sit around the kitchen table and listen to her music together as a family. summary: We expect the beta program to expand to more regions soon.

title: The Pixel 11 Pro is the wrong Pixel to buy this year
summary: The Pro has its upsides, but is it enough to justify the extra cost?
body: The new Google Pixel 11 series is a known quantity at this point. It comes with several new AI features like Gemini Intelligence , camera improvements, and the brand-new Tensor G6 chip. Although many Google fans are drawn to the beefier Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL, that doesn’t mean the Pro phones are the best pick for everyone. The base Pixel 11 might miss out on the extra features you’d get with a Pro, but you’ll save a fair chunk of change, and you are likely to find, at least when it comes to performance, that the phones are more alike than different.

title: The Galaxy S26 Ultra just achieved a first for Android phone sales
summary: Samsung is the sole Android brand in the top 10, but the S26 Ultra also made a notable achievement.
body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra was the most popular Android phone globally in Q2 2026, according to a new report. This is apparently the first time that an “ultra-premium” phone led Android sales in Q2. The base Galaxy S26 also made the list, along with three Galaxy A phones. The most popular Android phones in a quarter tend to be cheap models. That’s not a surprise, as the lower prices make these phones more accessible than high-end models. However, the latest global market share report reveals a surprising top-seller for Android. Counterpoint Research has posted its Q2 2026 global market share report , and it turns out that the $1,300 Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra was the most popular Android phone in the quarter. Samsung’s Ultra phone was ranked fourth. What’s also interesting is that the base Galaxy S26 landed in ninth place. By contrast, the Galaxy S25 Ultra was in ninth place back in Q2 2025 while the base S25 didn’t feature at all.

The experience will also feature a series of DJ sets, with the likes of DJ Target, DJ Manny Norté, DJ Semtex and DJ Esi taking over the decks from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. each day. The London double-header follows Jay-Z’s three-night run at Yankee Stadium in New York City, which took place in July. Across the shows, the rapper was joined by a star-studded line-up of guests that included Beyoncé, Alicia Keys, Usher, Eminem, Nas, Pharrell Williams, Rihanna, Slick Rick and more. title: Hate the new Google Photos UI? Here’s how to fix the worst thing about it
summary: Bring back the dates!!
body: If you’ve used Google Photos for years , as I and probably most people reading this have, there are certain features and creature comforts you’ve likely come to rely on. For me personally, one of those is seeing my photos organized by the date they were taken. It’s a simple thing, but I love it. I like quickly scrolling through my Photos feed and knowing exactly when certain pictures or videos were captured. It helps me remember what I was doing on that specific date and keeps my app feeling nice and organized.

body: TL;DR TECNO’s 0mm-bezel concept has been shown off in a hands-on video, offering the clearest look yet at the phone ahead of its IFA 2026 showcase. The bezel-less design looks impressive but comes with a usability trade-off, as the raised frame can catch your finger during gesture navigation. The concept features a 144Hz display, triple rear cameras, a 6,000mAh battery, and a holographic, lenticular back panel TECNO has built a reputation for showcasing unusual smartphone concepts at major tech events. The PHANTOM Ultimate G Fold , billed as the world’s thinnest trifold, debuted ahead of IFA 2025, while MWC 2026 brought an ultra-thin modular phone . Now, a hands-on video of TECNO’s latest concept phone is out, giving us our first proper look at its bezel-less design ahead of its IFA 2026 debut. TECNO itself showcased the 0mm-bezel phone a few weeks ago, teasing its edge-to-edge display without revealing much about what it would be like to actually use. That has now changed, with Marques Brownlee (MKBHD) going hands-on with the device. He also showed it from multiple angles while putting its unusual design to the test.

title: Google’s smartest Pixel 11 Pro feature is already driving me crazy
summary: A bright idea gone dim.
body: I’ve only had the Pixel 11 Pro XL for a few days, and somehow that’s still been enough time for it to remind me why I’ve had trust issues with Pixels all year. I really do try to give these phones a fair shot. I look for the good stuff, I get excited about the new features, and every time, I hope this will finally be the Pixel that doesn’t make me question my life choices a few days in. This time, HiLight is doing the damage. And the annoying part is that I actually love the idea. It reminds me of the notification LEDs we used to have back in the day. I was quite excited to play around with it on my Pixel 11 Pro XL because, honestly, I’ve missed having something like this on a phone. Then I actually tried using HiLight.

title: Google Photos may soon give you less time to restore deleted media
summary: Google could soon unify trash retention rules and cut the recovery window for backed-up files from 60 days to 30 days.
body: Credit: Taylor Kerns / Android Authority TL;DR Google Photos currently keeps backed-up media in the Trash for 60 days and regular, non-backed-up media for 30 days. Code found in Google Photos v7.90 indicates Google plans to unify this rule, reducing trash retention for all media to 30 days. The change is not yet live, but it will likely be announced with plenty of notice before rolling out broadly. Google appears to be preparing a notable shift in Google Photos, shortening the time deleted photos and videos sit in your trash folder before they vanish forever. While Google has been spotted working on smarter backup solutions, such as overnight backup options , this upcoming change could rationalize how long your discarded media hangs around. title: Lenovo’s first Android handheld lets you stream PC games without a network connection
summary: No network for game streaming? No problem.
body: Credit: Lenovo TL;DR Lenovo has launched the Legion Cloud Gaming Handheld C700 in China. The handheld has a dongle that allows you to stream games from a PC without a network connection. Expect to pay ~$327 for this Android handheld. The Android handheld space has become highly competitive, as companies like ANBERNIC, Retroid, and AYANEO all duke it out with interesting products. Now, Lenovo has decided to step into the arena with a newly launched Android handheld of its own. Lenovo launched the Legion Cloud Gaming Handheld C700 in China this week, coming months after we first heard about it . This is a huge Android handheld designed for (surprise) cloud gaming. The device supports “one-touch” streaming from a PC via Lenovo’s proprietary Legion Stream protocol and an included dongle. In fact, the company says you can stream games while offline. That could be handy if you’re traveling.

title: Life360 adds new pet care tools to help keep your household in sync
summary: The shared care logs might stop your dog scoring a second dinner.
body: Credit: Life360 TL;DR Life360 is rolling out new pet-related features, including shared care logs that help families track routines such as feedings. The update also brings some lighter extras, including Weekly Roundups and Zoomies Alerts. A new $7.99 Pet Tag lets someone who finds a lost pet contact its owner or share its location more easily. It’s apparently International Dog Day tomorrow, but you can be forgiven for forgetting — the timing lands right as many households are descending back into school-run chaos. This can make it a little tougher to keep track of who fed and walked your four-legged friend , but Life360 is keen to simplify things with some new shared pet-care features. As detailed in the press release , the new Care and Connection tools are rolling out now, with Shared Care logs doing a lot of the heavy lifting. Families can set recurring routines for walks, feedings, medications, litter cleaning, and more, while completed tasks are visible to everyone in the care circle. That should make it easier to see who has actually done what, and perhaps stop your dog from successfully convincing a second family member that dinner never happened.

Inside the box is the RG 55G1 and a user manual. As we learned earlier, the system will be available in three colors: Indigo, Retro Gray, and Black. title: Google Home automations not working right lately? Blame your TV
summary: Google Home automations aren't playing nicely with your TV, but Google is on the case.
body: TL;DR Google Home users are reporting automations tied to TV starters failing to run. Google confirms an investigation is underway into problems with TV-based automations. So far the reports we’ve seen involve TCL models, but it’s not clear if other brands are similarly impacted. If you’re looking to configure a really impressive smart home, Google Home automations are your best friend. While routines are great for pulling off complicated multi-device workflows, automations take that to the next level by, well, automating them — instead of manually activating a routine, automations begin all by themselves when their starter event occurs. At least, that’s the way things are supposed to work, but right now there’s a frustrating glitch impacting automations tied to TVs. Over on Reddit’s Google Home sub, users have been complaining about automations involving their TVs that fail to work . While you should be able to use events like powering your TV on or off to trigger an automation, Google Home just doesn’t seem to recognize when these starter events happen.

title: Frustrating Google Home bug refuses to add items to your shopping lists in Keep
summary: Another day, another Google Home bug.
body: TL;DR Some Google Home users are facing a bug where the voice assistant refuses to add items to their Google Keep lists. While not all users appear to be facing this issue, it appears widespread enough for Google to take notice. Meanwhile, a quick look at Google Home settings suggests that access to notes & lists using a voice assistant may have been removed. It feels like we’re reporting on a Google Home bug or a fix almost every other day. Only today, users received some good news following reports of devices refusing to set alarms over voice commands. Sadly, those good times aren’t going to last, and it now looks like yet another function is being impacted by a similar glitch, as some people are seemingly unable to add items to their lists on Google Keep using Google Home voice commands. In a series of complaints on Reddit, including one from Friday, a user claims the voice assistant recognizes their commands perfectly well, but refuses to add items to the list . For instance, if the person asks one of their Google Home devices to “add x to list xyz,” the assistant might respond by saying how many items are on that list, while refusing to add any new items.

Play Services and Play Store receive several smaller improvements. Google’s last Play Services update brought us a busy mix of changes, including hints of Googlebook multi-device setup and expansion of Tap to Share to include links. Now, another update is rolling out, continuing the Googlebook push while giving Gemini-powered Ask Play more attention. Google Play Services v26.33 and Play Store v52.9 are the fourth system services updates rolling out this month. While much of the latest Play Services changelog is aimed at developers, there are a couple of standout changes.

summary: Let the iPhone comparisons begin.
body: TL;DR Samsung’s Galaxy S27 Ultra has recently had its layout detailed through some CAD leaks. Those files are now being used to render some high-quality images of how the phone could look. The S27 Ultra seems to be embracing a whole new camera system. Is Samsung actually trying something new in the design department for next year’s Galaxy S27 Ultra? While many of the company’s recent year-to-year refreshes have felt relatively minor, leaks have suggested that Samsung could be thinking about trying out a bold new look for the S27 series, with renders this week depicting the S27 Ultra showing off an unusual new camera design . Now we’re getting an even better look at this layout, thanks to the publication of some new CAD-based renders. Ahead of actual imagery of a new phone surfacing, sometimes we get our first look by way of pictures generated from detailed measurements of the hardware — the kind of info a case maker might use to develop their products ahead of a phone’s launch. When those leak, they can be used to create the sort of flat, basic 3D renderings we saw in yesterday’s S27 Ultra leaks . But now Android Headlines has teamed up with leaker Steve Hemmerstoffer to dress thi…

title: Super Smash Bros. is ready for its unofficial Android port
summary: You can't play it on Switch, but unsanctioned Android ports could be coming soon.
body: TL;DR Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 64 has been fully decompiled, opening the door to unofficial native ports. The 1999 platform fighter hasn’t been available through official means for several years and isn’t currently playable on Nintendo Switch consoles. We aren’t aware of any ports made from the newly decompiled code yet, but we expect they’ll start appearing soon. Aside from some high-profile rereleases, present-day Nintendo is notoriously stingy when it comes to providing easy, legitimate access to its immense back catalog of classic games. This, in part, has inspired fans to take matters into their own hands by decompiling old favorites, recreating their source code so the games can be easily (if unofficially) ported to modern platforms like Windows or Android. Now, another classic that’s been inaccessible on modern hardware is ripe for porting: 1999’s Super Smash Bros. has been fully decompiled. As shared on Decomp.dev , Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 64 is now “100.00% decompiled,” meaning the game’s source code has been completely recreated and it’s ready to be ported. Compared to emulated games, ports created from decompiled source code can run natively on modern hardw…

title: Google is working on a big Live Translate upgrade for Android XR
summary: Listening area in Google Translate may offer extensive control over the Live Translate feature for Android XR-based devices.
body: TL;DR Google Translate could introduce big Live Translate updates for the Android XR platform. We have exclusively uncovered traces of a “Listening area” feature that will offer extensive control over the microphones. If implemented, users will be able to switch between Front-only and Surrounding-area mic modes for Live Translate on Android XR. While there’s only one Android XR device on the market right now, namely the Samsung Galaxy XR, there are more on the way. Google has already built deep integrations for its core apps like Google Maps, Photos, Gboard, and the Play Store. Last year, we uncovered development on Live Translate for Google’s extended reality platform. We can now exclusively reveal a potential feature addition for the Live Translate experience on Android XR. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. Authority Insights brings you all the latest exclusive reports, app teardowns, leaks, and in-depth tech coverage from the Android Authority team that you won’t find anywhere else.

title: The next wide-screen foldable may have just leaked in real-world images
summary: New leaked images offer a closer look at Xiaomi’s mysterious wide-screen foldable.
body: TL;DR Xiaomi’s next foldable has leaked, showing a wide inner display and a design that closely resembles the company’s own HyperOS 4 teaser. The XRing O3 will power the device, with a 10-core CPU, Arm’s new G2-Ultra NX GPU, and eye-catching performance claims. The Xiaomi 18 Fold launches in September, but key details such as global availability, pricing, and dimensions remain unknown. Xiaomi’s XRing O3 chipset has already made headlines with some seriously ambitious performance claims, but the chip’s first phone may be just as interesting. Xiaomi has confirmed that the 3nm processor will debut in the Xiaomi 18 Fold next month, and now leaked images appear to show the company’s upcoming foldable in the flesh. The images, which Digital Chat Station (DCS) shared on Weibo , show a book-style foldable with a wide inner display similar to the Galaxy Z Fold 8 , relatively thick bezels, and a punch-hole selfie camera near the upper-right corner. One image also shows the rear of the device, including a large camera module, but it doesn’t reveal enough to say much about its hardware.

title: WhatsApp two-step verification codes are ditching six-digit PINs for full passwords
summary: WhatsApp is making some security upgrades, including turning two-step verification codes into full passwords instead of the traditional six-digit numerical PIN.

summary: Wyze is refreshing its 360-degree Indoor Cam Pan with an improved design and better night vision, and a price of just $40.

title: Nothing unveils Nothing OS 5.0 built on Android 17, but there’s bad news for older phones
summary: Older phones will not be receiving this update, as expected.
body: TL;DR Nothing has announced Nothing OS 5.0, bringing a massive overhaul featuring the Geist typeface, translucent software layering, dynamic wallpaper-tinted adaptive themes, and dedicated apps for both the Glyph Interface and Essential Apps Builder. The update also introduces Android 17 platform features such as split notification and Quick Settings panels, cross-platform Quick Share with iOS, enhanced privacy indicators, and more. Open Beta testing for the Nothing Phone 3 starts tomorrow, with a full stable release expected in mid-October. However, Phone 1, Phone 2, and CMF Phone 1 will not receive the update. Nothing has officially revealed Nothing OS 5.0, detailing the next major evolution of its custom Android skin. Built on top of Android 17 , the platform update brings a visual design overhaul, expanded lock screen personalization, new first-party widgets, and tighter system-level integration with the Glyph Interface. Following an announcement teased on X , Nothing published a detailed breakdown of the new features and the design evolution on its community forums.

title: New leak suggests Qualcomm’s next Snapdragon 8 Elite could take it to the extreme, literally
summary: Qualcomm's naming convention is getting further out of hand.
body: TL;DR According to a new leak, Qualcomm’s next flagship chip will be called the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. It could feature two prime cores clocked at 5.01GHz, along with three performance and three efficiency cores. The Dimensity 9600 Pro could also use two prime cores clocked at 4.55GHz, along with three performance and three efficiency cores. Qualcomm and MediaTek are both gearing up to launch their latest flagship processors. The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 series and the MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro are expected to feature improvements across the board. Now, a new leak is shedding some light on the core arrangement and clock speeds of the top-of-the-line Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and the Dimensity 9600 Pro. According to a Weibo post by Digital Chat Station (DCS), the upcoming Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro, model number SM8975, could be called the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 instead. The extremely long (pun intended) and unnecessarily weird name notwithstanding, Qualcomm’s next flagship chip seems set to break the 5GHz barrier for smartphone chipsets.

title: Galaxy S26 series gets sixth One UI 9 beta release, but when is the stable update coming?
summary: The latest 851MB update targets several UI and routine issues for global users ahead of the stable launch.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung has released the sixth One UI 9 beta for the Galaxy S26 series. The 851MB update (firmware ZZHE) includes the August 5, 2026, security patch and fixes key issues, including display errors with the Now Brief widget and photo-saving issues in Expert RAW 24MP at specific focal lengths. Currently live in Germany, India, Poland, the UK, and South Korea, the new update will soon be available in the US as well. Samsung entered One UI 9 development with much gusto, but after releasing the stable update alongside the new Galaxy Z8 foldables, the pace of One UI 9 beta releases for its previous flagships has slowed down a bit. After releasing the fifth One UI 9 beta almost two weeks ago, Samsung is now picking things up with the sixth One UI 9 beta release for the Galaxy S26 series. We’ve received the sixth One UI 9 update on our Galaxy S26 Ultra in the UK. This Android 17-based update comes with firmware version ending in ZZHE, the August 5, 2026 security patch, and is 851MB in size.

title: 5 reasons I may not go back to Spotify after trying YouTube Music
summary: YouTube Music isn't perfect, but you can't ignore the value proposition.
body: As is the case with millions of users around the world, I’ve been a loyal Spotify subscriber for as long as I can remember. The app works well across Android and iOS, there’s a great selection of music, and features like Jam and Spotify Connect have made my listening experience much more seamless across audio devices at home. I was happy to pay for the Premium Duo plan — until it was sneakily taken away. Spotify removed the Duo plan in India around November 2025, but as I had subscribed to it long before, I was able to continue with it, as it should be. Then came the email, one July morning this year, saying my Premium Duo plan was canceled due to an “issue” with my payment method. Nothing had changed, so it didn’t make any sense. I figured it was Spotify forcing me to upgrade to a higher-priced plan, and as it turned out, I wasn’t the only one who got the boot. Frustrated with this move, I decided to try other options.

title: After just 5 days, my Pixel 11 Pro is already a brick
summary: This isn't a great start.
body: The Pixel lineup and hardware woes seem to go hand in hand. Whether it’s OLED tint issues with the Pixel 2 XL, overheating, spontaneously shattering camera glass, or display issues with the Pixel 9 Pro lineup, hardware troubles seem constant. As a day-one Pixel user ever since the first phone launched, I’ve usually been immune to all the troubles that tend to plague Google’s flagship. Well, as the saying goes, luck eventually does run out. I’ve had my Pixel 11 Pro for just five days, and it’s already a brick. A couple of days into my time with the Pixel 11 Pro (in the gorgeous Canyon colorway), I decided to do a factory reset and a fresh setup instead of copying over all my data from my previous phone, and here we are.

title: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 has a camera problem, and it has nothing to do with photo quality
summary: Samsung put the Galaxy Z Fold 8's folding display selfie camera in the worst spot.
body: I’ve spent years trying the latest book-style foldables, but none earned a permanent spot in my pocket once I finished testing them. Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 7 came the closest with a thin-and-light design and truly flagship specs. Unfortunately, it suffered from the same problems as every other folding phone with a squarish inner screen aspect ratio. The form factor isn’t conducive to widescreen video content, as you’ll see large black bars at the top and bottom of the folding screen. Samsung built the wide Galaxy Z Fold 8 to specifically address this pain point, and it quickly won me over. Then, something happened that I didn’t expect. I found myself using the Galaxy Z Fold 8 unfolded in portrait orientation more than landscape.

title: Sony’s new phone is one of your only options with microSD support, but it’s not all roses
summary: Hey Sony, how about upgrading something?
body: TL;DR The Xperia 10 VIII is official with the exact same hardware as the Xperia 10 VII. It comes with the Snapdragon 6 Gen 3, 8GB of RAM, and 128GB of storage. The cameras are also exactly the same as the Xperia 10 VII, and the display is 50% brighter. After a couple of leaks , Sony has finally announced the new Xperia 10 VIII, and it’s basically the same phone as the Xperia 10 VII, bar one small upgrade and a new paint job. The Xperia 10 VIII looks almost exactly the same as the Xperia 10 VII. There’s the horizontal camera bar on the back, “Sony” branding on the camera island, and a front that looks remarkably out of date with thicker bezels on the top and bottom. It also retains the fingerprint scanner and the 3.5mm headphone jack, and Sony claims that the stereo speakers are now 30% louder.

title: We tried Gemini’s new Device Help feature on the Pixel 11, and the results were mixed
summary: Gemini is ready to fix your Pixel, well, almost ready.
body: TL;DR Gemini’s experimental Device Help feature is appearing in the Gemini app on Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro devices, letting you troubleshoot your phone using natural language. It can diagnose battery and Wi-Fi issues, open specific settings, change things like brightness and dark mode, and explain Pixel features without making you hunt through Settings. It’s still a Labs feature and can get things wrong. Our testing produced inconsistent instructions for Magic Capture, so it isn’t completely reliable yet. A few days ago, we spotted Google testing a clever new Gemini trick that could save Pixel users from digging through the Settings app every time something goes wrong. That feature, called Device Help, is now appearing directly inside the Gemini app on some of our Pixel 11 series devices. First spotted by 9to5Google , Device Help is currently showing up on Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro models we’ve checked, including our Pixel 11 Pro XL units. It still has a “Labs” badge attached, though, which is Google’s way of telling you things may not always work as expected. And after putting it through a few tests, that’s exactly what we found.

title: Google’s Tensor G7 has one last chance to save the Pixel 12
summary: Dubious silicon is detracting from Pixel's best features.
body: The Pixel 11 series has left Google with something of a dilemma. Based on our time with the phones so far, they remain among the most enjoyable Android handsets to use, thanks largely to Google’s software experience and a growing collection of genuinely useful features. But our testing of the Tensor G6 shows that Google’s custom silicon is falling further behind rival flagship chips; early gaming tests suggest a familiar litany of issues; and a week with the Pixel 11 Pro suggests that many of Google’s newest AI tricks aren’t yet strong enough to make up the difference. That’s not necessarily a problem for the Pixel 11, but it could become one for the Pixel 12.

title: Spotify has good news if your audiobooks suddenly stopped playing
summary: But some are still unable to play chapters despite the reported fix.
body: TL;DR Spotify experienced an outage that prevented listeners from playing or downloading audiobooks across multiple devices. The issue has officially been marked as resolved, though a few users report that playback glitches remain. Users still affected should update the app and report the issue on the Help board. Spotify has been steadily adding more reasons to spend time with audiobooks, from narrated magazine articles to TV-style recaps and Playlist Notes . But today, some listeners were unable to play those audiobooks at all, and Spotify now says the problem has been fixed. The issue surfaced earlier today, with Reddit reports coming from users across phones, desktops, and the web. Spotify acknowledged the problem through its Community forum, saying it had received reports that audiobook playback was not working properly and that the relevant teams were working on a fix.

title: The AYN Odin 3 is getting another price hike, but you can avoid it by acting fast
summary: You'll need to act fast to avoid the price increase.

This is still the only Android handheld with what is effectively the Snapdragon 8 Elite chipset, though. The AYN Odin 3 is the most powerful Android handheld on the market right now, making it ideal for cutting-edge emulation and other demanding games. It’s already seen price hikes this year due to the RAM crisis, but we’ve now got more bad news. AYN announced on Discord that it’ll be raising the price of the Odin 3 once again. These price hikes vary from $20 to $30. Check out the new prices below.

title: Spotify bug leaves Android Auto drivers staring at error message
summary: Spotify not working for you on Android Auto? You're not alone.
body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Android Auto users are reporting issues with Spotify. The app is displaying an error message that reads “Spotify isn’t responding.” It’s unclear what the cause of the problem is. Sometimes being an Android Auto user can feel like playing a game of whack-a-mole. A bug appears, a fix is rolled out, and another bug appears shortly after. For example, a fix for a glitch that caused connections to drop or freeze was recently released . Now, a new bug has shown up, and it’s preventing users from streaming their music and podcasts. According to several Android Auto users on Reddit ( 1 , 2 ), the latest issue affects the Spotify app. When attempting to access the app, these users are running into an error message that reads “Spotify isn’t responding.” The screen includes options to exit the app or to wait for it to start working again.

title: The Pixel 11 Pro XL is built to last and easy to fix, teardown finds
summary: It's pricey, but at least you'll be able to hold onto it a few years.
body: TL;DR JerryRigEverything’s Zack Nelson has tested the Pixel 11 Pro XL’s durability and repairability. The phone didn’t bend in Nelson’s durability test, and key components are relatively simple to swap out. Nelson calls the Pixel 11 Pro XL “one of the easiest phones to repair of 2026.” It looks like it should be relatively easy to make the Pixel 11 Pro last. The XL version has now undergone the JerryRigEverything treatment, and the phone held up nicely to Zack Nelson’s usual battery of abuse. The teardown video also shows that common repairs should be relatively simple, with both the display and the battery removable with just a few minutes of work. The video shows that the 11 Pro XL barely bends or flexes at all as Nelson wrenches on it, so the phone should hold up fine in case you sit down with it in your back pocket. Despite Google’s claim that the 11 Pro’s display is “more than twice as scratch-resistant than previous models” thanks to a new coating, though, it still scratches at level six with deeper grooves at a level seven.

title: Netflix is reportedly in talks to add rival streamers like Peacock
summary: Netflix could soon open up its service to other streamers.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Netflix could soon let you access other rival streamers through its platform. The company is reportedly in talks with Peacock and Fox One. It’s unclear if Netflix would sell subscriptions to those streamers or just include their content directly in the app. From Peacock to ESPN , there’s been a rash of streaming-related price hikes lately. If you’re worried that this article will be about Netflix announcing a rate increase, you can rest easy. That’s not happening, at least not yet anyway. Rather, this has to do with Netflix reportedly opening up its service to its rivals. It appears that Netflix is interested in becoming a one-stop shop for streaming. The New York Times reports that Netflix is considering adding shows and movies from other streaming services. The company is said to be currently in talks with Peacock and Fox One to bring their content to the platform.

title: The Galaxy S27 Ultra may debut with self-healing glass
summary: Android Authority remembers the LG G Flex 2.
body: TL;DR A rumor claims glass used in the Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra could come with a self-healing layer that fills in minor scratches on its own. The glass is purportedly being developed jointly by Corning and Samsung. The Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra may introduce an interesting feature that sounds like it could be a real benefit to users. A rumor from this weekend claims that Samsung’s upcoming Ultra flagship will come with self-healing glass that’s able to recover from minor scratches on its own. Late last week, industry observer Schrödinger took to X to say that Corning and Samsung are jointly working on “ a new self-healing surface coating” for the next iteration of the former’s Gorilla Armor glass. This coating would certainly be less scratch-resistant than conventional tempered glass, but if it’s able to fill in hairline scratches on its own, that trade-off could be worth it.

title: Apple’s 20th anniversary iPhone could take some inspiration from Android phones
summary: A leaked render of the 20th anniversary iPhone reveals a radical new redesign, with some familiar elements.
body: TL;DR Apple may be prepping radical design changes for the 20th anniversary iPhone, according to a new leak. The leaked renders show curved glass on the front and back with two horizontally placed cameras at the back. We’re also seeing what appears to be a hole-punch selfie camera on the screen, reminiscent of present-day Android phones. The iPhone is expected to see a radical shakeup this year, with Apple’s first-ever foldable likely to be revealed during the fall event next month. However, the company will reach a bigger milestone in 2027, marking 20 years since the first iPhone was revealed in 2007. A new leak is giving us our first potential look at the next-gen iPhone model Apple could introduce to celebrate. Leaker Yogesh Brar shares a couple of images on X that appear to show the 20th anniversary iPhone from multiple angles, including a clear view of its sides. It also appears to show a quad curved display on the front and a similarly curved glass on the rear panel. The images reveal dual rear cameras positioned horizontally, rather than vertically as on the iPhone 17. But for as interesting as all that is, it’s also hard to ignore some of the discrepancies in this particul…

title: ESPN’s streaming plans are getting more expensive: Here’s what you’ll pay
summary: Bundles including Disney Plus and Hulu are also affected.
body: TL;DR ESPN streaming plans and bundles are increasing in price. Plans are increasing by $1 to $3 per month. Adjustments also affect many streaming bundles that include ESPN. Last week, we learned that Verizon will soon increase the prices for its Disney Plus, ESPN, and Hulu perks , with plan add-ons increasing by a buck or two per month starting in September. Now, ESPN has announced that its streaming subscriptions and the bundles they’re included in will be going up in price for everyone, not just Verizon subscribers. As we’ve learned from 9to5Mac , ESPN has announced price hikes for its ESPN Select and ESPN Unlimited streaming plans. Select is increasing from $13 to $14 per month (or $140 per year, up from $130), while Unlimited is jumping from $30 to $32 per month (or $320 per year, from $300). Bundles including ESPN along with Disney Plus and Hulu are going up, too.

title: Microsoft will pay you to get your friends using Edge
summary: Get 500 points for every successful referral.
body: TL;DR Microsoft is rolling out a referral program that gives Edge users 500 Microsoft Rewards points for every successful referral. You can earn up to 7,500 points per month, worth roughly $6.82 toward Microsoft or Xbox gift cards. Referrals only count when a new Edge Mobile user installs through your link and searches with Edge on two different days within 14 days. Microsoft really wants you to try out its Edge browser — and it’s willing to put its money where its mouth is. The tech giant has previously awarded Edge usage over competing browsers with monetary incentives, and it is now paying users for convincing others to make the switch.

title: Galaxy Ultra power users should feel right at home on next year’s S27
summary: The S Pen will apparently still be on the left.
body: TL;DR Leaked renders of the Galaxy S27 Ultra show the phone could come with an iPhone 17 Pro-style rear camera island. Additional renders imply other aspects of the phone’s external hardware will be largely unchanged from Galaxy S26 Ultra. The S27 Pro, S27+, and standard S27 will apparently see other, minor design tweaks. With Samsung’s new foldables and Google’s Pixel 11 series here, the next major release to look forward to in the US Android market is the Galaxy S27 series, which should debut in early 2027. This morning, we got a look at early leaked renders of the Galaxy S27 Ultra , which show us that Samsung seems to be taking pretty direct design inspiration from Apple’s latest Pro iPhones. Now, we’re taking a look at yet more renders that show the phone from more angles. Superleaker Ice Universe has posted a handful of renders on X, showing that “Aside from the redesigned camera layout,” the upcoming S27 Ultra “will look nearly identical” to this year’s Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, with the same display size, left-hand S Pen placement, and more. The other S27 phones will apparently see some other minor layout changes, however.

title: YouTube is bringing lots more content types to 24/7 Stations feeds
summary: Tuning you in to some new ideas for Stations.
body: TL;DR YouTube introduced Stations earlier this year, featuring 24/7 content streams from musical artists. Now Google is expanding Stations to also include podcasts, creator content, and more. Access is only getting started with a small number of creators initially. Like any good streaming service, YouTube is always working to find the next big hook that will keep viewers glued to their screens, video after video. Earlier this year, we spotted a fresh addition to YouTube’s offerings in the form of Stations , 24/7 streams that appeared designed to connect you with an endless feed of content from your favorite musical artists. And now, Stations are getting a bit of an expansion. YouTube is constantly trying out new experiments, and this month, the service shares that its latest involves building Stations around even more diverse content than just music. While you’ll still see Stations from musical performers, they’re also starting to expand to cover podcasts, media channels, and just regular creator content.

title: Gemini on Pixel 11 Pro testing ‘Device help’ tool
summary: On the Pixel 11 Pro, we’re seeing a new “Device help” tool for the Gemini app that provides personalized and conversational assistance with your phone.

title: Philips Hue is working on a more affordable TV sync box
summary: It's apparently a lot less expensive, but it won't do as much.
body: TL;DR A UK retailer has listed the unannounced Philips Hue Play Sync Box Lite. The new version offers only a single HDMI input, among other compromises. The Lite model is listed at retailer Very for £109.99 compared to the existing premium model’s £299.99. The Philips Hue Play HDMI sync box 8K lets you synchronize your smart lights with what’s happening on your TV to create a “fully immersive light syncing experience” (as Hue puts it), matching the color and brightness of your smart lights with your video content in real time. It’s cool, but it’s also wildly expensive at an MSRP of $385. Now, though, it looks like Philips Hue is set to release a new, stripped-back version at a more affordable price. As spotted by Hueblog , UK retailer Very has published a listing for an unannounced sync box from Philips, the Hue Play Sync Box Lite. The Lite version is shown as having one HDMI input (to the current model’s four), meaning you’ll be limited to syncing lights with a single device’s video. It’ll apparently be much less expensive, though: the Hue Play Sync Box Lite is listed at £109.99, about a third the price of the 8K model’s £299.99 UK MSRP.
